19: A skill for converting uploaded UI screenshots and design mocks into pixel-perfect, functioning frontend prototypes and Google Golden Template React applications.

21: ## Why This Skill Exists

12: # Agent API
13: 
14: `agentapi` is a CLI that talks to the running language server, so anything that
15: can run a shell command can drive the agent. Use it when the caller is *not* the
16: agent itself, for example from a sidecar.
17: 
18: > [!NOTE] **Scope & Related Tools**: Don't use `agentapi` for communicating with
19: > subagents inside an active agent turn (use `invoke_subagent` or `send_message`
20: > instead).
21: 
22: ## Quick Start
23: 
24: Subcommand             | Command
25: :--------------------- | :------
26: **Start conversation** | `agentapi new-conversation "<prompt>"`
27: **Send message**       | `agentapi send-message "<conversation-id>" "<message>"`
28: **Read metadata**      | `agentapi get-conversation-metadata "<conversation-id>"`
29: **Discover commands**  | `agentapi help` / `agentapi <command> help`
30: 
31: ## Discovering commands
32: 
33: The CLI is self-documenting, and its help output is generated from the live
34: command registry.
35: 
36: ```bash
37: agentapi help            # every command, with usage
38: agentapi <command> help  # description and examples for one command
39: ```
40: 
41: ## Common usage
42: 
43: ```bash
44: # Start a new conversation with a prompt.
45: agentapi new-conversation "Summarize my unread email and flag anything urgent"
46: 
47: # Send a message to another conversation, or to your own to notify yourself.
48: agentapi send-message "<conversation-id>" "Build finished, results are in /tmp/out"
49: 
50: # Read metadata for a conversation.
51: agentapi get-conversation-metadata "<conversation-id>"
52: ```
53:

80: - **`P2-SURFACE-CONTRAST`**: Card background and border tokens blend into the canvas or reverse the reference polarity.
81: - **`P2-FONT-CATEGORY`**: Sans-serif used where the comp uses a high-contrast editorial serif or monospace numeric ticker (`tabular-nums`).
82: - **`P2-RADIUS-SHADOW`**: Border radius differs by more than one Tailwind step (e.g. `rounded-none` vs `rounded-2xl`) or heavy drop shadows obscure clean 1px hairlines.

87: 
88: ```text
89: Cycle 1: Synthesize Golden Template React files -> Build -> Render -> Audit
90: Cycle 2: Fix all P0 (collisions, overflow, macro grid tracks, missing assets)
91: Cycle 3: Fix all P1 (button padding symmetry, equal card widths/heights, line counts)
92: Cycle 4: Fix all P2 (exact hex tokens, border opacity, font weights, radius)
93: Cycle 5+: Fine-tune spatial coordinates using rendered_overlay.png until s_total >= 0.85

97: - Track `s_total` after every cycle.
98: - If an edit **reduces** `s_total` or increases `collision_count`, revert that specific CSS/JSX change immediately and inspect `rendered_overlay.png` to see which coordinate shifted in the wrong direction.

# Interaction, Story & "How It Feels" Evaluator (`interaction-eval`)

40: 1. **stop and judge on every stage**:
41:    - `dev-agent` never rushes straight from initial JSX generation to final delivery in one unverified pass.
42:    - At each stage (`image-to-react`, `responsiveness`, `interaction`, `feel`), `dev-agent` runs multiple turns, stopping at the end of each turn to run that stage's **dev eval** until every hard gate passes.
43: 2. **mirror every passed dev eval into `design-agent`**:
44:    - Passing a dev eval is necessary but not sufficient. Immediately after passing any dev eval on the dev side, `dev-agent` runs the **same stage as a designer critique** going back into `design-agent` (via `design-critique`), anchored to `design-agent`'s original inspiration (`taste` + `atlas` + reference sources).

46:    - Adding a slider in `interaction` or tuning drawer springs in `feel` must never break `t=0` visual match (`image-to-react`) or `320px` overflow (`responsiveness`). Whenever `dev-agent` patches code for a later stage or a `design-agent` request, it re-verifies upstream dev gates before advancing.

1: # Custom Agents
2: 
3: Custom agents allow you to define tailored execution contexts for the Jetski
4: Agent. You can configure them with custom system prompts, specific tool sets,
5: and even arbitrary executable logic.
6: 
7: A Custom Agent can be used in two ways:
8: 
9: *   **Custom Main Agent**: Replaces the default Jetski agent for the workspace
10:     session.
11: *   **Custom Subagent**: Spawned from another agent using the `invoke_subagent`
12:     tool to delegate specialized tasks (e.g., code review, linting, deep
13:     research).
14: 
15: ## Implementation Styles
16: 
17: There are three ways to define a custom agent:
18: 
19: 1.  **Markdown Agent (`agent.md` — Preferred)**: A single Markdown file defining
20:     the agent's YAML frontmatter and system prompt body. Automatically includes
21:     standard default prompt sections (`user_information`, `mcp_servers`,
22:     `skills`, `messaging`, `artifacts`, `guidelines`, `communication_style`,
23:     plus `subagents`).
24: 2.  **Declarative Agent (`agent.json` + `config.yaml` with `agent_config:`)**: A
25:     directory containing an `agent.json` manifest pointing to a `config.yaml`
26:     file using the canonical `agent_config` schema. Required when an agent needs
27:     internal Google3 prompt sections (`google_identity`,
28:     `google_user_information`, `google3_infrastructure`, `user_rules`,
29:     `conversation_transcript`), custom prompt section selection or interleaving,
30:     or `cascade_config` runtime overrides.
31: 3.  **Interactive Agent (Executable)**: A directory containing an `agent.json`
32:     manifest pointing to an executable binary or script that handles the
33:     interaction loop over stdin/stdout.
34: 
35: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
36: 
37: ## 1. Markdown Agents
38: 
39: Markdown agents are the standard, recommended way to define a custom agent. They
40: can be de

257: ## 3. Interactive Agents (Executable)
258: 
259: Interactive agents run as persistent external processes. They are useful when
260: you need complete control over the agent's reasoning loop or need to integrate
261: with external systems.
262: 
263: ### Manifest (`agent.json`)
264: 
265: ```json
266: {
267:   "name": "custom-loop-agent",
268:   "description": "Runs a custom execution loop for specialized tasks.",
269:   "command_spec": {
270:     "command": "blaze",
271:     "args": ["run", "//path/to/your/agent:binary"]
272:   }
273: }
274: ```
275: 
276: *   **`command_spec.command`** (string, required): The executable to run.
277: *   **`command_spec.args`** (array of strings, optional): Arguments to pass to
278:     the executable.
279: 
280: ### Execution Loop and SDK
281: 
282: Interactive agents receive `init` metadata and turn `input` requests line-by-line over stdin from the Jetski Language Server, and communicate back via Connect RPC over HTTP (or gRPC) to deliver messages (`SendAgentMessage`) and signal turn completion (`SignalExecutableIdle`).
283: 
284: To simplify development, use the **Antigravity Python SDK**
285: (`//third_party/jetski/sdk/py/interactive.py`), which provides helpers like
286: `run_persistent` and decorators for registering custom tools and lifecycle
287: hooks.

1: # JSON Configuration Files
2: 
3: JSON configuration files allow you to explicitly register and manage
4: customizations that are stored outside the default discovery locations (such as
5: project-specific folders or shared team directories in Piper).
6: 
7: Each customization type has its own configuration file, placed in your
8: customization root directory (e.g., `_agents/` in google3, or
9: `~/.gemini/config/` globally, or within a plugin):
10: 
11: *   **Skills**: `skills.json`
12: *   **Rules**: `rules.json`
13: *   **Agents**: `agents.json`
14: *   **Sidecars**: `sidecars.json` (within plugins)
15: *   **Plugins**: `plugins.json`
16: 
17: Inside a workspace, these files are honored in every `_agents/` or `.agents/`
18: directory between the current working directory and the workspace's
19: customization root, so a config file at the repository root applies no matter
20: which subdirectory a session is started in. Relative `path` entries resolve
21: against the directory containing the dot-dir that declares them, falling back
22: to the repository root when nothing exists there.
23: 
24: ## Configuration Schema
25: 
26: All configuration files share the same schema, allowing you to declare path
27: entries and inherit from other configurations.
28: 
29: ```json
30: {
31:   "exclude": ["global-deprecated-skill"],
32:   "inherits": [
33:     {
34:       "path": "/google/src/head/depot/google3/experimental/team/shared_skills/skills.json",
35:       "include_only": ["linter-skill"],
36:       "exclude": ["deprecated-skill"]
37:     }
38:   ],
39:   "entries": [
40:     {
41:       "path": "google3/java/com/google/myteam/skills",
42:       "exclude": ["experimental-.*"]
43:     },
44:     {
45:       "path": "~/personal-skills"
46:     }
47:   ]
48: }
49: ```
50: 
51: > [!NOTE] `rules.json` is the recommended way to share rule content across
52: > directories or teams. Rules it registers keep their frontmatter and t

148: ### Pro-Tip: Stable Team Sharing in Google3
149: 
150: When sharing configurations across a team, you want them to work regardless of
151: whether a team member is in an active workspace or using a global surface.
152: 
153: *   **The Shared Config (Checked into Piper)**: Store your team's skills/agents
154:     in a central directory (e.g., `google3/experimental/team/shared/`) and
155:     create a `skills.json` there pointing to them.
156: *   **The User Subscription (Local Global Config)**: Teammates should reference
157:     the shared config in their global `~/.gemini/config/skills.json` using a
158:     **read-only depot snapshot path**:
159: 
160:     ```json
161:     {
162:       "inherits": [
163:         { "path": "/google/src/head/depot/google3/experimental/team/shared/skills.json" }
164:       ]
165:     }
166:     ```
167: 
168:     Using `/google/src/head/depot/google3/...` ensures the path is always
169:     resolvable by the Jetski backend, even if the user has no workspace open.

1: # Plugins
2: 
3: Plugins are namespaced, shareable bundles that package **Skills**, **Agents**,
4: **Rules**, **Hooks**, **Sidecars**, and **MCP Server Configurations** into a
5: single deployable unit. They are the recommended way to distribute complex,
6: feature-rich customizations to your team.
7: 
8: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9: 
10: ## Directory Structure
11: 
12: A plugin must be contained within a subdirectory of a `plugins/` folder in a
13: customization root (e.g., `_agents/plugins/` in google3).
14: 
15: ```text
16: plugins/<plugin_name>/
17: ├── plugin.json       # Required: Manifest file
18: ├── README.md         # Optional: Human-facing docs, shown in the Marketplace
19: ├── mcp_config.json   # Optional: MCP servers exposed by the plugin
20: ├── hooks.json        # Optional: Lifecycle hooks run by the plugin
21: ├── agents.json       # Optional: Root-level agents configuration
22: ├── rules.json        # Optional: Root-level rules configuration
23: ├── skills.json       # Optional: Root-level skills configuration
24: ├── sidecars.json     # Optional: Root-level sidecars configuration
25: ├── rules/            # Optional: Rule directory
26: │   ├── AGENTS.md     # Recommended consolidated rules file
27: │   └── <rule_name>.md # Individual rule markdown files
28: ├── skills/           # Optional: Skill directory
29: │   └── <skill_name>/ # Individual skill directories
30: │       └── SKILL.md
31: ├── agents/           # Optional: Custom agents exposed by the plugin
32: │   └── <agent_name>.md # Markdown agent (or legacy <agent_name>/agent.json)
33: └── sidecars/         # Optional: Background processes, including UI panes
34:     └── <sidecar_name>/
35:         └── sidecar.json
36: ```
37: 
38: -----------------------------------

120:     *   **Sidecars** in `plugins/<name>/sidecars/` or referenced via
121:         `plugins/<name>/sidecars.json` are discovered and managed by the Sidecar

123: 
124: ## Registering Plugins
125: 
126: Plugins can be discovered automatically if placed in standard customization
127: roots, or they can be explicitly registered using `plugins.json`.
128: 
129: *   See the [JSON Configurations Guide](./json_configs.md) for details on how to
130:     use `plugins.json` to enable specific plugins or inherit them from shared
131:     team paths.
132: 
133: ## Turning Plugins On and Off
134: 
135: Most discovered plugins are **enabled by default**; a plugin can ship switched
136: off by declaring `"disabled": true` in its `plugin.json`, and some built-in ones
137: do. Whether a plugin is active is recorded in the user's `config.json`, under a
138: `plugins` map keyed by the plugin's **directory** name:
139: 
140: ```json
141: {
142:   "plugins": {
143:     "my-plugin": { "enabled": false }
144:   }
145: }
146: ```
147: 
148: The setting can be changed from the plugin section of the settings UI, or from
149: the CLI's `plugin enable` / `plugin disable` subcommands, both of which write
150: this entry.
151: 
152: `config.json` wins wherever it has an entry, so a user's choice always beats
153: what the plugin declares. A plugin with no entry falls back to its `plugin.json`
154: declaration, which is how a plugin that ships disabled stays off until the user
155: turns it on. Jetski never records a preference inside the plugin itself, so the
156: choice survives reinstalling or updating the plugin.
157: 
158: A disabled plugin still appears in the plugin list so it can be turned back on,
159: but none of its bundled customizations are loaded.

1: # Google Skill Specification & `validate_skill.py` Rules
2: 
3: Every skill wrapped by `skill-maker` is checked against the exact rules enforced by `//learning/gemini/agents/skills/skill_creator/scripts:validate_skill`.
4: 
5: ## 1. Required Files in Every Wrapped Skill Folder
6: 
7: | File | Purpose | Required by `validate_skill` / `skill_creator` |
8: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
9: | `SKILL.md` | YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`, optional `metadata`) + imperative workflow instructions | **Mandatory** |
10: | `BUILD` | Blaze `agent_skill`, `validate_skill_test(check_locked_links = True)`, `eval_suite`, and `exports_files` | **Mandatory for Google3** |
11: | `EVAL.txtpb` | `EvalSuite` textproto (`learning/gemini/agents/evaluation/evalin/proto/eval_suite.proto`) with 3+ task cases | **Mandatory for Evalin** |
12: | `TEST.md` | End-to-end human and automated smoke test plan | **Mandatory** |
13: | `references/contributing.md` | Core invariants, editing principles, and verification commands (linked from `## Contributions` in `SKILL.md`) | **Mandatory when `## Contributions` present** |
14: | `scripts/BUILD` | `pytype_strict_binary` rules for `.py` scripts and `exports_files` for `.mjs` scripts | **Mandatory when `scripts/` present in experimental/team skills** |
15: | `skill.json` | Structured metadata (`id`, `title`, `domain`, `summary`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `references`, `commands`) | **Mandatory for Skills Portal & `x20`** |
16: | `evals/smoke.json` | Deterministic smoke verification case | **Mandatory for Skills Portal** |
17: | `index.html` | Self-contained dark/light HTML documentation & preview page (`x20` opaque-origin safe) | **Mandatory for `x20` folder browsing** |
18: 
19: ## 2. Hard `validate_skill.py` Invariants
20: 
21: 1.  **Frontmatter Keys**:
22:     -   Only allowed keys: `name`, `description`, `license`, `allowed-tools`, `metadata`, `compatibility`, `support_tier`, `version`, `tags`, `category`, `disable-model-invocation`, `disable-slash-command`, `type`, `title`, `resource`, `timestamp`, `okf_version`.
23: 2.  **`name` Field**:
24:     -   Must match `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, length `<= 64`, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`.
25: 3.  **`description` Field**:
26:     -   Must use `>-` block scalar.
27:     -   Length `<= 1024` characters.
28:     -   **No `<` or `>` characters anywhere in `description`** (for example, write `at least 0.93` instead of `>= 0.93`, and `{slug}` instead of `<slug>`).
29:     -   No `[TODO:` placeholders.
30: 4.  **Line & Byte Limits**:
31:     -   Soft warning threshold: `500` lines / `35,000` bytes.
32:     -   Hard failure ceiling: `800` lines / `46,080` bytes (`view_file` truncation limit).
33:     -   Minimum cardinality: `>= 50` lines (unless backed by `references/*.md`).
34: 5.  **Outbound Links in `SKILL.md`**:
35:     -   Forbidden prefixes: `file:///`, `/google3/`, `/google/src/`.
36:     -   Every relative link (`references/...`, `scripts/...`, `examples/...`, `assets/...`) must exist on disk inside the skill directory.
37: 6.  **Contributions Link**:

"### 1.3 intentional timing, ambient settle & easing curves (`01-warm` tokens)
- **press & hover tokens**: `80ms` press tint/opacity (stable button width, zero layout shift) and `120ms` fine-pointer hover (`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`, no overshoot; hover never commits selection or fires network requests).
- **route & small state changes**: `160ms` route crossfade, `180ms` small state changes, `220ms` expanded content, and `240ms - 420ms` smooth deceleration (`cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`) for sheets/drawers (exits `20%-30%` faster).
- **ambient illustration & 4-second settle rule**: decorative programmatic 2D/SVG/canvas or shader motion stays strictly inside `pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden` illustration layers, plays at most one `4s` intro swell before settling to the `t=0` still (never replaying on typing, focus, or tab return), exposes a keyboard-operable `Pause` button whenever continuous motion exceeds `5s` (WCAG 2.2.2), and suspends via `Page Visibility API` when offscreen, hidden, or covered by a modal/keyboard.
- **editorial chapter settles**: `<= 550ms` with restrained travel (`8px - 14px` max), clearing `transform` / `will-change` after settle (`data-landed="true"`) so serif and body text stay razor-sharp.
- Never use robotic `linear` easing on spatial UI movement (reserve `linear` strictly for timecodes, progress bars, or continuous marquees)."

5: ## 1. Required Files in Every Wrapped Skill Folder

7: | File | Purpose | Required by `validate_skill` / `skill_creator` |

14: | `scripts/BUILD` | `pytype_strict_binary` rules for `.py` scripts and `exports_files` for `.mjs` scripts | **Mandatory when `scripts/` present in experimental/team skills** |
15: | `skill.json` | Structured metadata (`id`, `title`, `domain`, `summary`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `references`, `commands`) | **Mandatory for Skills Portal & `x20`** |

17: | `index.html` | Self-contained dark/light HTML documentation & preview page (`x20` opaque-origin safe) | **Mandatory for `x20` folder browsing** |

20: 
21: 1.  **Frontmatter Keys**:
22:     -   Only allowed keys: `name`, `description`, `license`, `allowed-tools`, `metadata`, `compatibility`, `support_tier`, `version`, `tags`, `category`, `disable-model-invocation`, `disable-slash-command`, `type`, `title`, `resource`, `timestamp`, `okf_version`.

25: 3.  **`description` Field**:
26:     -   Must use `>-` block scalar.
27:     -   Length `<= 1024` characters.
28:     -   **No `<` or `>` characters anywhere in `description`** (for example, write `at least 0.93` instead of `>= 0.93`, and `{slug}` instead of `<slug>`).
29:     -   No `[TODO:` placeholders.
30: 4.  **Line & Byte Limits**:
31:     -   Soft warning threshold: `500` lines / `35,000` bytes.
32:     -   Hard failure ceiling: `800` lines / `46,080` bytes (`view_file` truncation limit).
33:     -   Minimum cardinality: `>= 50` lines (unless backed by `references/*.md`).

35:     -   Forbidden prefixes: `file:///`, `/google3/`, `/google/src/`.

A readiness check (`ready_ok`) will ensure images are complete, have valid dimensions, and are free from corruption or decoding errors. A retina resolution check (`density_ok`) will confirm that images meet the required 2x density, based on either DOM-mounted size or target dimensions for standalone assets. An anti-blur check (`sharp_ok`) will evaluate sharpness through Laplacian variance and a roundtrip sharpness ratio. Sharpness will be assessed by downscaling, then upscaling an image. Low Laplacian energy change indicates a blurry upscale, signifying "fake" 2x pixels. Absolute edge acutance will be checked using a Sobel gradient and Laplacian standard deviation with a smooth-gradient exemption. A sharpness gain check will be performed against a low-res crop if available, alongside color drift validation. Aspect ratio correctness will be validated. The agent will compare intrinsic aspect ratio to client-side dimensions, accounting for `object-fit` CSS properties, to prevent image distortion during DOM rendering.

7: # Details that make interfaces feel better
8: 
9: Great interfaces rarely come from a single thing. It's usually a collection of small details that compound into a great experience. Apply these principles when building or reviewing UI code. Before suggesting or writing a fix, identify the project's existing styling system and express the change in that system: Tailwind in a Tailwind project, plain CSS in a CSS project, or the established CSS-in-JS approach. Never introduce a second styling system just to apply a polish fix.
10: 
11: When reviewing, slow the interface down: replay motion at 10% speed in the browser's Animations panel and walk every state: hover, focus, active, loading, empty. What feels off at 10% speed is what's subtly wrong at full speed.
12:

14: 
15: | Category | When to Use |
16: | --- | --- |

19: | [Animations](animations.md) | Interruptible animations, enter/exit transitions, icon animations, scale on press, motion restraint |
20: | [Icons](icons.md) | Icon stroke weight, states via `currentColor`, outline vs fill, sizing, RTL flipping |

27: Outer radius = inner radius + padding. Mismatched radii on nested elements is the most common thing that makes interfaces feel off.

6: # Breaking UI
7: 
8: ## Initial Response
9: 
10: When this skill is first invoked without a specific question, respond only with:
11: 
12: > I'm ready to throw the worst realistic data at your UI and show you what breaks, my standards come from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy.
13: 
14: Do not provide any other information until the user asks a question.
15: 
16: An adversarial skill. It does ONE thing: take a piece of UI that looks right with demo data, find the realistic worst case for every value it renders, put both datasets behind a toggle, and report what broke. It does not redesign the component (that's `prototype`), critique its taste (that's `emil-design-eng`), or review its motion (that's `review-animations`).
17: 
18: ## Operating Posture
19: 
20: You are the most annoying real user this component will ever meet. Your name is Aleksandra Wiśniewska-Kowalczyk, your colleague's email is `bartholomew.fitzgerald@northwind-industries-holdings.example.com`, your intern is called Jo, and your workspace has 1,284 members. None of that is contrived. Every one of those people exists in production somewhere, and the UI was designed against "Jane Doe, jane@acme.com, 12 members".
21: 
22: Demo data is chosen, usually without anyone noticing, to make the design look good: names that fit on one line, counts that never need a separator, every optional field filled in. The job here is to undo that choice, one field at a time.
23: 
24: Two failure modes, and the first is worse:
25: 
26: 1. **Nonsense data.** `"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"` and 5,000-character names prove nothing. The designer will rightly say "that never happens" and stop listening. Every worst-case value must be something a real user could plausibly produce, or the longest value the backend actually accepts.
27: 2. **Stopping at long text.** Long names are the obvious break. The ones that ship are the short name that leaves an orphaned dash, the missing avatar, the count of exactly 1 ("1 members"), the empty list, the badge whose text got translated.

88: ## Designing Inline Widgets (Cards & Transparency)
89: 
90: When embedding inline in chat (`<agent-embed>`), style widgets as native chat
91: components:
92: 
93: *   **Transparent Root Background**: Always set `<body class="bg-transparent
94:     ...">` so the widget blends seamlessly into the chat container.
95: *   **Card-Based Layouts**: Wrap inline content and controls in a card container
96:     (as shown in the Boilerplate Template above) to provide elevation and
97:     prevent loose text in light mode.
98: *   **Standalone Artifacts**: For full-page side-pane artifacts (like
99:     dashboards), use a solid background (e.g., `bg-[var(--background)]`).
100: 
101: ## Sizing Inline Embeds
102: 
103: For inline embeds, it is important to think **small and compact**.
104: 
105: Inline embeds only have a **500px** height viewport. Past that the widget
106: scrolls inside a small box and the user sees only a fragment of what you built,
107: so don't build inlined widgets that are too tall.
108: 
109: *   **Do not set a `height` attribute on `<agent-embed>`.** It is ignored.
110: *   **Think compact** Think carefully about designing something that is compact
111:     and fits nicely inline in the chat height budget.
112: *   **If the idea genuinely needs more room, make it a standalone artifact.** A
113:     scrolling inline widget is usually wrong — full-height in the side pane
114:     beats cropped in the chat.
115: 
116: After generating the artifact, consider whether it is sufficiently compact to be
117: useful inline and adjust if needed.
118: 
119: > [!IMPORTANT] Never size an inline widget relative to the viewport: no
120: > `h-screen`, `min-h-screen`, `100vh`, or `height: 100%` on a top-level
121: > container. The frame's viewport is derived from your content, so these feed
122: > themselves and the widget collapses to a sliver. Use padding for breathing
123: > room instead.

"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Renames the dev-agent coordinator to jason-dev-agent across the skills workspace (idempotent)."""
import pathlib
import re
import shutil

ROOT = pathlib.Path("/usr/local/google/home/jfesta/skills")
EXTRA = [pathlib.Path("/usr/local/google/home/jfesta/.gemini/jetski/brain/df11f66f-0b19-40ca-92d8-6b17dde612c0/dev-agent-diagram.html")]
EXTS = {".md", ".py", ".json", ".html", ".mjs", ".txtpb", ".yaml", ".yml", ".ts", ".tsx"}
pat = re.compile(r"(?<![\w-])(?<!jason-)dev-agent")

# 1. rename agent files first
for base in ("_agents/agents", ".agents/agents"):
    old = ROOT / base / "dev-agent.md"
    new = ROOT / base / "jason-dev-agent.md"
    if old.exists():
        shutil.move(str(old), str(new))
        print(f"[MOVED] {old.relative_to(ROOT)} -> {new.relative_to(ROOT)}")

# 2. rewrite references
changed = 0
files = [p for p in ROOT.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and (p.suffix in EXTS or p.name == "BUILD")
         and "node_modules" not in p.parts and "dist" not in p.parts and ".eval_work" not in p.parts] + EXTRA
for p in files:
    try:
        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
        continue
    new = pat.sub("jason-dev-agent", text)
    if new != text:
        p.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
        changed += 1
        print(f"[REWROTE] {p}")
print(f"files rewritten: {changed}")
"

"# imported-plate refresh pass (rule for `jason-dev-agent` mode B)

**Rule.** When `jason-dev-agent` receives a folder (or zip) of plates that did **not** come from `design-agent`, it must re-output every plate through Nano Banana **before** `image-to-react` runs. The goal is only freshness and safety — the imagery `jason-dev-agent` builds from must be the most recently generated — never a redesign.

This pass is **not** used for `design-agent` studies (the harness path): those plates are already fresh Nano Banana 2 `2k` output.

## what the pass does

| rule | value |
| :--- | :--- |
| prompt | one very simple **mirror** prompt per plate (below) — no design change |
| quality | high quality, **>= 1k** long edge |
| size | **same exact pixel size** as the input (plates under 1k are lifted to 1k keeping aspect, and flagged) |
| format | **same format** as the input (`png` -> `png`, `jpg` -> `jpg`, `webp` -> `webp`) |
| speed | one call per plate, no polish rounds, no iteration — re-output quickly and move on |
| output | `<study>/nano/<pillar>/<same filename>` mirroring `concepts/<pillar>/<file>` |
| downstream | after verify, `selections.json`, `manifest.json`, and `index.html` point at `nano/`; `image-to-react`, `replicate-mock`, `responsiveness`, `interaction`, and `feel` all peer into `nano/` — `concepts/` stays as the untouched originals |

## the mirror prompt

```text
Re-output this exact UI design plate 1:1 as a fresh, clean, high-quality render.
Mirror it precisely: identical layout, grid, typography, copy, colors (same hex values), spacing,
imagery, crops, shadows, and corner radii. Do not redesign, restyle, add, remove, or move anything.
Only remove compression artifacts, dithering, and softness so every edge, glyph, and photo is crisp.
Same aspect ratio and framing; no borders, no watermarks, no captions.
```

"def drift_mae(a: pathlib.Path, b: pathlib.Path) -> float | None:
  """Mean abs RGB delta (0..255) between 8x8 box-downsampled versions of two images."""
  try:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["magick", "compare", "-metric", "MAE",
         "(", str(a), "-colorspace", "sRGB", "-alpha", "remove", "-filter", "box", "-resize", "8x8!", ")",
         "(", str(b), "-colorspace", "sRGB", "-alpha", "remove", "-filter", "box", "-resize", "8x8!", ")", "null:"],
        capture_output=True, text=True)
    txt = (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip()
    val = float(txt.split()[0])
    return round(val / 65535.0 * 255.0, 2) if val > 1.0 else round(val * 255.0, 2)
  except Exception:
    return None"

12: # Agent API
13: 
14: `agentapi` is a CLI that talks to the running language server, so anything that
15: can run a shell command can drive the agent. Use it when the caller is *not* the
16: agent itself, for example from a sidecar.
17: 
18: > [!NOTE] **Scope & Related Tools**: Don't use `agentapi` for communicating with
19: > subagents inside an active agent turn (use `invoke_subagent` or `send_message`
20: > instead).
21: 
22: ## Quick Start
23: 
24: Subcommand             | Command
25: :--------------------- | :------
26: **Start conversation** | `agentapi new-conversation "<prompt>"`
27: **Send message**       | `agentapi send-message "<conversation-id>" "<message>"`
28: **Read metadata**      | `agentapi get-conversation-metadata "<conversation-id>"`
29: **Discover commands**  | `agentapi help` / `agentapi <command> help`
30: 
31: ## Discovering commands
32: 
33: The CLI is self-documenting, and its help output is generated from the live
34: command registry.
35: 
36: ```bash
37: agentapi help            # every command, with usage
38: agentapi <command> help  # description and examples for one command
39: ```
40: 
41: ## Common usage
42: 
43: ```bash
44: # Start a new conversation with a prompt.
45: agentapi new-conversation "Summarize my unread email and flag anything urgent"
46: 
47: # Send a message to another conversation, or to your own to notify yourself.
48: agentapi send-message "<conversation-id>" "Build finished, results are in /tmp/out"
49: 
50: # Read metadata for a conversation.
51: agentapi get-conversation-metadata "<conversation-id>"
52: ```
53: 
54: When calling `agentapi new-conversation` or `agentapi send-message` from inside
55: an active agent's shell tool (where `ANTIGRAVITY_SOURCE_METADATA` is inherited
56: with an empty `project_id`), prefix with `env -u ANTIGRAVITY_SOURCE_METADATA`
57: to avoid `cross-project messaging is not allowed: sender project "" does not
58: match recipient project "<id>"`.

# accessibility

```text
jason-dev-agent / accessibility
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
scope      type sizes, line height, contrast, target sizes, focus, names, alt, lang
standard   wcag 2.2 aa (hard) · aaa / apple hig / material (recommended, reported)
eval       scripts/eval-accessibility.py  (live dom in headless webkit, exit 0/1)
when       stage 1a gate, re-run after stage 2 / 3 / 4, before every design talk-back
```

Design plates set the look; this skill guarantees the shipped **font sizes, line heights, contrast, and button/target sizes** meet accessible standards — and when a plate's value cannot meet them, `jason-dev-agent` raises it to `jason-design-agent` as a developer with the number that must move (never silently restyles).

"# WCAG 2.2 type, contrast & target rules with css recipes (`accessibility`)

## text size & line height

| token | hard floor | recommended | recipe |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| body (`p`, `li`, `td`, `label`) | `14px` | `16px` / `1.5` | `text-base leading-relaxed` (16/1.625) or `text-[15px] leading-[1.6]` |
| small / caption / eyebrow | `12px` | `12px` + `tracking-[0.02em]`+ | `text-xs tracking-[0.14em] uppercase` only for `<= 3` words |
| ui labels in buttons / pills | `13px` | `14px` | `text-sm`; never `text-[11px]` |
| headings | — | `line-height >= 1.1`; `h1 >= 1.5x` body | `text-5xl leading-[1.05]`, `text-3xl leading-tight` |
| measure | — | `45–75ch` body, `<= 90ch` max | `max-w-prose` / `max-w-[65ch]` |

- Text must survive 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) and the user overrides in 1.4.12 (line height `1.5`, paragraph spacing `2x`, letter spacing `0.12em`, word spacing `0.16em`) **without clipping** — avoid fixed heights on text containers with `overflow: hidden`; prefer `min-h-*`.
- Use `rem`-based sizes (Tailwind defaults) so browser font-size preferences scale the page.

## contrast

- Normal text `>= 4.5:1`, large text (`>= 24px`, or `>= 18.66px` at weight `>= 700`) `>= 3:1` (WCAG 1.4.3). AAA: `7:1` / `4.5:1` (1.4.6).
- Non-text: control borders, focus rings, icon strokes, and state indicators `>= 3:1` against the adjacent background (1.4.11).
- Fix at the token layer. Typical moves on a dark `#0c0c0b` canvas: muted ink `#858481` (4.1:1) → `#9a9994` (4.6:1); placeholder `#494946` is decorative only, never for required copy. On bone `#e7e4de`: muted `#787774` (3.6:1) → `#5e5a52` (5.4:1).
- Text over photography: add a scrim (`bg-black/40` or a gradient) or move text onto a solid panel; the eval reports `bg: image` nodes separately because contrast cannot be computed reliably — verify by eye and keep a scrim.

## target size

- WCAG 2.5.8 (AA): every pointer target `>= 24x24` css px **or** has `>= 24px` spacing to the next target; inline links inside sentences are exempt.

| numerals / prices / tables | secondary `tabular-nums` (or tertiary mono) | inherits | 500–600 | — | — |

## modular scale

Pick one ratio and derive everything from body (`16px`):

| ratio | name | body → small / h3 / h2 / h1 | use |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `1.2` | minor third | `16 → 13 / 23 / 28 / 33` (+ fluid hero) | product UI, dashboards, apps |

| `1.333` | perfect fourth | `16 → 12 / 28 / 38 / 51` | editorial, long-form |

"# Definition of Done & Handback Specification

A Golden Template React build is **Done** and ready for final `jason-design-agent` sign-off only when all 6 conditions are fully satisfied.

---

## The 6 Conditions for Done

1. **Lint Clean**:
   `node golden-template/scripts/lint-golden-template.mjs --dir=<study> --project=<item-slug> --fix` exits `0`. All 4 root config files and 4 source subdirectories strictly match the dating blueprint, with zero build-temp leaks and strict TypeScript passing.

2. **All Dev Stage Gates Green**:
   `python3 jason-dev-agent/scripts/run_dev_loop.py --project=<item-slug>` exits `0` (`ALL PASS`). Every carried-over skill (`nano-banana`, `font-pairing`, `accessibility`, `image-to-react`, `responsiveness`, `interaction`, `feel`, `verify_html_bundle`) passes its evaluation criteria.

3. **Comp Matching (`s_total >= 0.93`)**:
   Headless AutoRaterV1 64x64 cell loss scoring reaches `s_total >= 0.93` against the reference comp plate (`0` grid baseline delta, `0` asymmetric button padding, `0` overflow).

4. **Designer Approval Across Stages 1–4**:
   Every stage has been handed back to `jason-design-agent` via `Loop B` with concrete developer receipts and received designer sign-off.

5. **Dev Turns & Moodboard Updated**:
   `<study>/projects/dev-turns.json` reflects total, per-item, and per-stage dev turns. The `Development` view of `<study>/index.html` displays the `jason-dev-agent: <K> turns` header badge and the `dev · <n> turns` per-card pill with working `open build` links.

6. **Final Sign-Off Emitted**:
   Control is handed back to `jason-design-agent`, which writes `<study>/critique/final-design-signoff.md` evaluating the final build against both benchmark research dossiers and 2K concept plates.

"# The Dev Flywheel: Automated 5-Turn Source Check-Back Loop Specification
## Continuous In-Loop Refinement Against Reference Comp, Style Kit & Inspiration (40-Minute Timeout)

- **Author**: Principal Software Engineer, Google AI & Frontend Systems
- **Target**: `jason-dev-agent`

## 1. Motivation & Architecture

The **Dev Flywheel** is the developer equivalent of the design flywheel. Where the design flywheel prompt-steers concept plates, the dev flywheel is an **automated code-refinement engine** that continuously tests, diagnoses, and patches the live React DOM until all 5 source check-back gates pass.

It cross-references the live built DOM against **three canonical sources of truth**:

This document defines the exact interactive initialization protocol executed immediately upon launching `jason-dev-agent`.

---

## Interactive Launch Sequence

Upon activation (`"Activate jason-dev-agent"`), the agent immediately executes an interactive questionnaire via `ask_question` (or direct prompt) containing the following sequence:

1. **Question 1 (Curated Study Folder)**:
   - *Prompt*: `"Where is the curated design study folder or project directory? (Provide path to <study-slug> containing selections.json, plates, and style-direction)"`

2. **Question 2 (Build Scope Selection)**:
   - *Question*: `"Which approved components or screens would you like to build?"`
   - *Options*:
     - `(Recommended) All approved plates (selections.json with selected: true)`
     - `Specific plate or component (provide item slug)`

3. **Question 3 (Dev Flywheel & Frame Budget Settings)**:
   - *Question*: `"Would you like to configure the Dev Flywheel (source check-back loop) settings?"`
   - *Options*:
     - `(Recommended) Default (5 cycles, 40-minute timeout ceiling / 2400s, 60fps frame budget)`

# Activating and Using `jason-dev-agent` in Chat

Activation instructions and interactive intake protocols have been established for `jason-dev-agent`, matching the exact structure and clarity of `jason-design-agent`.

---

## 1. Activation Commands

To launch the developer agent in chat, type:

> **"Activate jason-dev-agent"**

*(Recognized trigger phrases: `"Run jason-dev-agent"`, `"Build with dev agent"`, `"Start jason-dev-agent"`)*

---

## 2. Interactive Launch Questionnaire

Immediately upon activation, `jason-dev-agent` initiates an interactive intake sequence via `ask_question` (or direct prompt) to configure the build:

1. **Curated Study Folder**:
   - *"Where is the curated design study folder or project directory?"*
   - Path to `<study-slug>` containing `selections.json`, 2K concept plates (`concepts/` or `nano/`), `style-direction/`, and `canon.md`.

2. **Build Scope Selection**:
   - *"Which approved components or screens would you like to build?"*
   - `(Recommended) All approved plates (selections.json with selected: true)`
   - `Specific plate or component (provide item slug)`

3. **Dev Flywheel & Frame Budget Settings**:
   - *"Would you like to configure the Dev Flywheel (source check-back loop) settings?"*
   - `(Recommended) Default (5 cycles, 40-minute timeout ceiling / 2400s, 60fps frame budget)`
   - `Fast Audit (1 cycle, skip auto-remediation)`
   - `Strict Production (Require 44px touch targets & explicit [data-scroll-point] hooks)`

4. **Preview Deployment Target**:
   - *"Where should the live compiled React bundle be previewed?"*
   - `(Recommended) Local Right-Hand Artifact Pane & localhost (Default)`
   - `Deploy to x20 web hosting (explicit request only)`

---

## 3. What Happens Next (Execution Flow)

```text
User: "Activate jason-dev-agent"
  │
  ▼
[Interactive Intake Questionnaire] -> Lock study path, scope, flywheel & preview target
  │
  ▼
[8 Simple Developer Steps]
  • Step 1: replicate-mock      (extract hex tokens, px measurements & 3 buckets)
  • Step 2: font-pairing        (primary H1-H3, secondary body/UI, modular scale)
  • Step 3: image-to-react      (React 19 DOM shell & AutoRaterV1 visual match)
  • Step 4: nano-banana         (target upscale-queue only -> 2x Retina)
  • Step 5: accessibility       (WCAG 2.2 AA contrast >= 4.5:1, 16px body floor)
  • Step 6: responsiveness      (single unified DOM across 6 viewports: 320px-1536px)
  • Step 7: interaction & feel  (0 dead controls, [data-scroll-point] hooks, 60fps)
  │
  ▼
[Step 7.5: The Dev Flywheel]
  • Continuously checks the 5 sources (Comp Plate, Style Kit, Captures)
  • Auto-patches code until all 5 pass or hitting the 40-minute timeout (2400s)
  │
  ▼
[Step 8: Golden Template Lint & verify_html_bundle.mjs]
  • Strict TypeScript compilation (tsc exit 0) & headless VM mount audit
  │
  ▼
[Designer Checkpoint]
  • PAUSE FOR HUMAN REVIEW: Displays build path, receipts table & clickable [Open Build] link
```
